My perspective deepened during my Doctorate at a university ranked in the global top 500, where I learned to connect careful assessment with realistic action. I am from France, and I have long been fascinated by the way bridges, roads, and public spaces influence how people move, connect, and experience their communities. It is this connection between technical design and public use that led me toward a career as a Civil Engineer, where I can combine problem-solving, creativity, and public impact in a practical way. I built my academic foundation through a Master’s degree at a university ranked in the global top 500, and through that training I developed a strong grounding in engineering analysis, design thinking, and project delivery. Across my studies and applied work, I completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in turning technical requirements into buildable solutions that balance safety, cost, and long-term performance. In particular, working through the constraints that shape infrastructure delivery encouraged me to look beyond calculations alone and focus on how sound design decisions hold up in real conditions.

Alongside this, I have learned how to adapt quickly when projects demand new knowledge. On one assignment, I needed to use a tool that was new to me, and after a few months of focused effort I was using it confidently enough to contribute productively to the team’s workflow. I have also dealt with recurring site and coordination issues in a practical way; when one repeated bottleneck was slowing progress, I helped put in place a workable alternative process that reduced delays for the team. In my own area, colleagues sometimes come to me with technical questions, and I value those moments because they often lead to clearer decisions and smoother coordination across different parties.

Beyond technical work, civil engineering feels personal to me. During a family road trip, we crossed a bridge I had helped deliver, and my relatives insisted on stopping for a photo while joking that it was the only vacation landmark where I could explain the drainage system in detail. That moment captured exactly why this profession matters to me. I am now eager to bring my training, practical mindset, and commitment to useful, resilient infrastructure to a Civil Engineer role while continuing to grow through meaningful projects.

One of my clearest personal memories is sitting at the kitchen table with a family member, assembling simple reading-game resources, then hearing the next day that the class had asked to play them again. That moment showed me how teaching can reach beyond a lesson and become something shared, meaningful, and lasting.

I also value working closely with colleagues; when asked for ideas or resources, I make a point of sharing what I have used and explaining what worked in practice.

Originally from Spain, I would now welcome the opportunity to bring this background, energy, and sense of purpose to a primary school community where I can contribute positively, keep learning, and help children grow in both confidence and understanding.
